story_overview: A girl named Lyra has a voice that bends reality — every song she sings reshapes the world around her in some way. She has been afraid of it her whole life, singing only in whispers. A traveling musician finds her and tells her the world is going silent — an ancient dissonance is spreading, muting all music, all sound, all life. Only a Songweaver at full voice can reverse it. The climax is Lyra singing — truly, fully, fearlessly — for the first time.

speech: She sang and the world listened. Not metaphorically. The stones turned. The water rose. The wind changed direction and waited for the next note.
The world was going silent. You could feel it in the air. The birds had stopped singing first. Then the wind. Then the voices of the people, one by one.
Lyra walked through the village with her hands over her throat. She had a voice that could bend reality. She had been afraid of it her whole life.

Where the note touched the ground, a flower bloomed. A single flower in a world of silence. It was not much. But it was something. And sometimes something is enough to start a song.

Her fingers strummed strings that made no sound. The lute was full of music. The world just could not hear it anymore.

The musician knelt. Her lips moved. No sound came out. But Lyra understood. 'I found you,' the woman said without saying. 'I have been looking for a very long time.'
Lyra took her hands away from her throat. The musician smiled. And somewhere in the silence, a note waited. It had been waiting for this moment for years.

speech: The final note faded. Lyra stood on the hill, exhausted, her voice raw, her body trembling. The world was green and blue and gold again. It was over.
